body:
Attempted to test it but couldn't get the buttons to do anything, plus Forward+ and Mobile render modes produced error spew that looked like this:
![Screenshot 2024-12-08 160707](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39267c6c-356d-4cd1-9dd5-77de8f14b1f9)

while the compatibility rendered failed differently:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac9dd8ed-5c91-4467-82cf-2a4637baacef)

Neither of these errors appeared when testing a build with the same configuration without this patch.

Additionally, I think the contrast of the buttons could be better in light mode and in general - it's a bit hard to distinguish when its hovered and pressed, as seen here:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/60f41931-44c0-4191-8de4-1d62e31de179

---

Specs:
Windows 11
AMD Ryzen 5700X3D
Geforce RTX 3070
compiled with `scons p=windows target=editor optimize=speed use_llvm=yes lto=thin scu_build=yes production=yes`

There was line in shaders I forgot to remove. I pushed the fix.

>  I think the contrast of the buttons could be better in light mode and in general - it's a bit hard to distinguish when its hovered and pressed, as seen here:

I wish it looked better too. But I'm not sure how to theme them better, the default appearance of buttons was already quite bad, so I had to make them flat, remove focus which was in the way, and use a PanelContainer to get a background, which also had no default so I picked gray. Maybe they could be made non-flat so that their background reflects their presset state better, but the default was very bad at that (hover was transparent for some reason? And pressed didn't look good. Also if I made the unpressed stylebox empty to make the pressed ones stand out, text no longer shows up on hover and pressed??). I wonder how I could pick the existing styleboxes, but tweak them slightly? Suggestions welcome.
EDIT:
Actually, turns out the theming weirdness I encountered only happened in my test scene. In editor, it works well, so I changed it:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8ef1fe7-8932-42b4-b1f3-27ac7421fb9e)

Also TextureLayered and Texture3D previews are not using containers, which has the side effect of not shrinking the channel selector when one of the color components is not available. I wonder how I can make it shrink.

I'm also considering to hide the selector if the image has only one channel. Though one minor thing, I use a mask to return available channels, and getting if there is only one bit set just means testing if it's a power of two, which is a simple integer calculation, and... `Math` has no function for that. The function is actually defined in `memory.cpp` so I wonder if I could just move it to `Math`.

> I'm also considering to hide the selector if the image has only one channel.

Yes, I'd hide it in that situation since there's no point in toggling the only channel present.

Works as expected now, after the changes!

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ccabc430-9b9b-4430-b4d4-33a896095e1a)
I prefer the solid colors when things are selected, but there's some weird borders with the styling right now that make it look a bit messy around the edges.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/134363b6-da80-4e43-9b02-7016e26c72be)
The unselected contrast is unchaged in light mode, so still not ideal.

Part of the problem is that theme defaults are bad, and I don't know how to fix that while keeping it look good with any colors.

This is what it looks like with defaults:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d893abe-f64e-4a52-a248-e140514e14d0

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/41a0a593-6cf0-4958-b167-016f21275c4c

Hover for some reason is very transparent (which is why I added a PanelContainer, which itself specifically has no background in the inspector (??) so I had to give it a color manually), and unpressed looks almost the same as pressed, or brighter (which is why I removed it).
I wish I could just tweak the original stylebox colors while somehow also going well with any theme colors, but I don't know how I can override that without having to remake them from scratch for these states?

If it's too difficult to make buttons look good, I could maybe revert to a clickable icon which pops a menu with 4 regular checkboxes, but the proposal (and myself) preferred direct buttons (and might still need to handle the icon looking good in all themes too)
Try using `some_button->set_theme_type_variation("FlatButton");` to use the same styling as the buttons in the 3D editor viewport (or `"FlatMenuButton"` but that one is meant for MenuButtons).

Here is how it looks with `FlatButton`: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8c8aa48-75a5-4ee0-8353-c97aa8d6eddd

Not really better, unless maybe I could bring back the background of PanelContainer, but it doesn't have one in the inspector for some reason. Is there another variation I could use?

Also even with `static` this `is_power_of_2` function really doesn't want to be defined more than once with GCC Oo I thought `static` was meant to avoid this? If not then I would have to move this somewhere like `Math` or `typedefs` with the other power-of-two functions

Will it look better with https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100569?
Also maybe you could try to override some theme styles for these buttons - for example, outline or shadows.

After a bit of investigation, it appears `PanelContainer` does have a stylebox, but it is invisible. I have no idea why that is the case.
So to workaround that, I tried setting up the background of `Tree`, combined with @Calinou 's suggestion:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df782869-68fb-4674-b658-b082c0b0eae7)

It still doesn't look good at all. It's hard to see which buttons are pressed.
I would need the same background color as the one used in the toolbar, as this is like a mini toolbar. But I don't know where to get that (it would be so much easier if the background from The control that is supposed to have one, was just there in the first place).

> Will it look better with https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100569?

I don't think this will affect things much.

> Also maybe you could try to override some theme styles for these buttons - for example, outline or shadows.

Been trying to do that for most of the work on that PR, it has to follow the user's theme as much as possible, so can't just hardcode something like I did initially. I have managed to get what I wanted very quickly in a test project without such hacks, but that missing background is in the editor's theme is making things confusing.

This time I tried with `TabContainer` `panel` and reduced its content margin, so colors are the same as the viewport toolbar:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d1287431-dccb-41d6-9150-630443b00591)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f4f89ab-fe20-4662-b38b-b658b9a42912)
I'm worried that those buttons will always block part of texture preview by default and user (me) have to resize side panel to move those buttons outside of texture bounds.

@arkology I had the same worry, but it also applies to everything else we layer on top of those previews (details label, layer selector in 3D/layered textures).
If we really want to address that in this PR too, I thought these controls could be placed below the preview instead of being layered on top. I don't know how they should be laid out though.
> but it also applies to everything else we layer on top of those previews Oh yeah, something really needs to be done about this:

We can make the button background translucent (~50% opacity) so it's less distracting. The buttons should remain easily visible nonetheless.

Regarding the issue where buttons are placed behind the information label, the buttons could be moved to the top to avoid this.

BTW please note that Camera3D preview and Subviewport will also be affected by this change.
And also not sure does it make sense to have the buttons in subresource preview like in comment above. I mean, how often it will be used?
I like this change, but it is hard to find proper place for it.

@Calinou this is how it looks like if I move it to the top and halve transparency:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a72dfacf-2508-47bc-aa9f-34b17deb4277)
It is more discrete but also it halves contrast so it is harder to see which buttons are active.

One other thing I thought about is to reduce the size of buttons. But I could not think of an easy way. AFAIK their minimum size comes from "content margin", which sounds like I would have to modify the style of every states of every button. I tried doing it anyways, setting all content margins to 0, it had no effect at all. It appears to be impossible to shrink them further, despite obvious margins above and below text.

@arkology Ah, forgot that TexturePreview has also been used for Camera3D and SubViewport... why is it the case? Barely anything is getting re-used, it just displays the texture and hides everything else. If the controls were not layered on top it could have been useful to have actually, but I guess I can hide them for now.
I'm not sure about removing that from the sub-inspectors. Those easily represent half of cases where I inspect stuff. And what about the other two controls? Also I'm not sure how I can even detect that the control is being used in a sub-inspector.
If we really want a safe spot, it could be below the preview. It will occupy a line though. 
Another possibility is a dropdown, shrinking the overlay to a 3-dot icon maybe, but that looses the ability to glance which channel is being filtered. 
Yet another possibility is an icon to toggle the presence of RGBA buttons.

With a line below the preview it looks like this:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/29cca4d4-7293-4873-a740-ace46a1e08fe)

With the togglable icon idea:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2e2497c-3647-430e-a219-be928a4e34f5)
Using a cube here from another resource previewer, but we could imagine it could be some kind of "4 layers" icon.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/93eeded6-63ea-445c-9791-4626d3c1341b)

No idea what to do about these messages :/ I think they weren't present before. I always rebase when syncing and always amend my commit when making changes...
My branch only has one commit:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ddf0d129-54f6-4dd8-bfef-ae046be1b3f1)
If there is an unwanted commit, I'm not seeing it anywhere.

@Zylann Strange, this is what I see on my end at the bottom of the PR:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/026d7eac-2370-4cf7-b091-3e419e11f8b2)
Ah, I no longer see it either. Not sure what happened.

I'm agreeing a bit with the fact this control might be a little too present, even with half-transparency.
Do you think it would be better to put it behind a toggle like this?

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2e2497c-3647-430e-a219-be928a4e34f5)

> Do you think it would be better to put it behind a toggle like this?

I have an idea that in future there could be context menu where visibility of such things as this one and metadata label (and so on) could be toggled. Like, you press RMB on texture and context menu appears.
But for now I think that hiding these buttons behind toggle is the solution.
Perhaps they don't even need to be created in constructor, but when you press a switch (maybe this is already done, I didn't look at code ATM).

> I'm agreeing a bit with the fact this control might be a little too present, even with half-transparency. Do you think it would be better to put it behind a toggle like this?

IMO it should be, the image previews are already pretty small, so space should be conserved as much as possible.

Changed to wrap with a toggle button. I added a new icon for it.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05d96f9b-bb57-4e1d-a611-b54eca3a14c0)

I also realized the outline added by #100569 is drawn with the texture preview itself, so the filter ends up applying to it too. So I made it drawn by another control on top.
Thanks!
